standard_prerequisites.name: The Count sentence
standard_prerequisites.statement: The second-order sentence Count, asserting existence of an inductive subset containing z and closed under u that covers the domain, is true in a structure exactly when its domain is enumerable; the unit establishes this before the counted theorem.
standard_prerequisites.use: It converts the negated Count sentence into the assertion that the domain is nonenumerable (572-578).

standard_prerequisites.name: Nonenumerable sets exist
standard_prerequisites.statement: There are nonenumerable sets, for instance the power set of the naturals or the reals, as established by Cantor's diagonal argument.
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the infinite models of the negated Count sentence (578-582).

core_obligations: Recall the Count sentence and its reading: it is true in a structure exactly when the domain is enumerable, so its negation holds exactly of structures with nonenumerable domain (572-578).
Nonenumerable structures exist: take any nonenumerable set, such as the power set of the naturals or the reals, as the domain of a structure (578-582).
Conclude that the negated Count sentence has infinite models, namely the nonenumerable structures, but no enumerable models, so the Loewenheim-Skolem property fails for second-order logic (582-584).

proof_roadmap.step: Recall the enumerability sentence and negate it.

difficulty_reason: The counted theorem is the author theorem at source lines 567-570: there are second-order sentences with infinite models but no enumerable models. The author proof (572-584) exhibits the sentence negating the unit's Count sentence, which expresses enumerability of the domain in second-order logic, and observes that structures with nonenumerable domains, such as the power set of the naturals or the reals, satisfy it; the negated Count sentence then has infinite models, namely the nonenumerable ones, and no enumerable models. The strength of the example rests on the earlier established reading of Count, which the proof recalls and uses.
